title: The Litany of Loreto
hookLine: a long chant of Mary's titles
tomorrow: Tower of ivory, house of gold

cards: Holy Mother of God. Pray for us. Mother most pure.
Pray for us. Seat of wisdom. Pray for us.
Morning star. Pray for us. One voice calls, the room answers, and the rhythm rolls on, name after name, like waves on a beach.

Some parishes sing it on a Saturday evening; some families say it after the rosary, half asleep on the couch. It's called a litany, and this one takes its name from a small hill town in Italy. Today's word: Loreto.

teach.h: LORETO: A SHRINE TOWN IN ITALY.
teach.b: Loreto is a shrine town in Italy. Tradition says it holds the Holy House, the house of Nazareth where Mary lived, and pilgrims come to pray there.
This litany was sung at that shrine, and the Church came to call it by the town's name. Its shape is call and response.

teach.h: HAVE MERCY ON US, THEN PRAY FOR US.
teach.b: It opens by turning to God: Lord, have mercy; Christ, have mercy; and to the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, with the answer, have mercy on us. Then it turns to Mary, and the answer changes to pray for us.
That small switch holds the whole Catholic understanding of Mary's place: mercy is asked of God; Mary is asked to pray. The names come in families.
Mother: Mother of Christ, Mother of the Church, Mother most amiable. Virgin: Virgin most prudent, Virgin most faithful.
Pictures borrowed from scripture and old poetry: Mirror of justice, Seat of wisdom, Mystical rose, Ark of the covenant, Gate of heaven, Morning star.
Help in trouble: Health of the sick, Refuge of sinners, Comforter of the afflicted, Help of Christians. And Queen: of angels, of apostles, of martyrs, of peace.
The list keeps growing. Popes have added names over time; Pope Francis added Mother of mercy, Mother of hope, and Solace of migrants.
Why so many? Because one name never covers anyone you love. A mother gets called all sorts of things in a single day, depending on what you need from her.
The litany does the same, out loud, together.

how: Catholics pray the Litany of Loreto in churches and at home, sometimes after the rosary or at Marian devotions; a leader calls each title and everyone answers, pray for us.

games.q: the leader calls, Mother most pure. what does the room answer?
games.why: to Mary's titles the answer is pray for us. have mercy on us is kept for the opening, addressed to God.

practice: If you pray, say five names from the litany slowly and answer each yourself: Seat of wisdom, pray for us; Health of the sick, pray for us; Refuge of sinners, pray for us; Comforter of the afflicted, pray for us; Queen of peace, pray for us.
Let a face come with each one, someone sick, someone grieving, someone far from home. If you don't pray, say the five names and let each one rest for a breath.

wordCard.voice: Loreto. A shrine town in Italy, and the name of the litany sung there: Mary's titles, called and answered, pray for us.

carryVoice: Your line: many names. Mercy is asked of God; Mary is asked to pray. I'll be here tomorrow.
